Contract: Private shell artifact capability door-stream-v1 must include doorstream/service.py and doorstream/motion.py. The image supplies python3-opencv offline and provides the service an exact RAM-backed credential directory containing camera fields plus validated public detector values: effective enabled and calibrated booleans, sample FPS, normalized minimum area, persistence/dwell/stationary bounds, normalized trigger/road zones, at most 32 masks serialized in at most 4096 literal ASCII bytes, and diagnostics. Effective enabled is true only when configured enabled=true, calibrated=true and every detector field validates without shell/AWK escape reinterpretation; tracked and SIM defaults are false/false. Runtime credentials/socket are unlinked only after a bounded runtime mask, stop/kill/reset sequence and stable settle interval positively verify both the unit and dedicated service identity inactive. Sanitized application motion observations carry generation and sequence only; no frame, URL, address or credential enters that event.

v1 panel-local audio socket at {$WALL_AUDIO_SOCKET}; Unix only, peer-UID checked, mode 0660, bounded concurrent clients and read deadline, newline-delimited JSON capped at 16384 bytes. Request {id,method,params,generation}; methods are status/telemetry/discover/cancel/pair/connect/disconnect/forget/select_input/select_output/set_visualizer. Response echoes id and a JavaScript-safe persistent generation and contains either {ok:true,result} or {ok:false,error:{code,message}}. Mutation authorization is an injected callback and defaults deny. Backend calls run in killable bounded child processes; deadline expiry terminates and reaps the child before capacity is returned. Mutations atomically persist intent before dispatch and result after success, deduplicate the last completed request across restart, and keep every post-intent exception sticky-uncertain. Results follow method-specific positive schemas; telemetry carries only bounded derived active/RMS/peak/bands and monotonic time, is stamped with the retained broker request epoch, and is rejected if a mutation advances that epoch during capture; neither path exposes colon/hyphen/underscore/compact/Cisco-dotted hardware addresses, including pairing confirmation, BlueZ paths, or raw/encoded audio. The default image backend reports backend_unavailable for mutation methods and unavailable telemetry until physical feasibility establishes bounded BlueZ/PipeWire authority.

Contract: v1 AI CLI service (SR-019, A40 ratified 2026-09-09). POST /v1/ask on {$AI_CLI_BIND}:{$AI_CLI_PORT} - loopback or the docker bridge ONLY, never the LAN - with {route, schema, messages}: `route` names a row in agents.registry.csv that is ALSO in routes-enabled (the registry is the catalog, the enable-list is the consent, an absent enable-list is 'no routes'), `schema` is REQUIRED and becomes the CLI's --json-schema, and `messages` is a user/assistant array rendered onto the child's stdin. MODEL AND DEPTH ARE NOT REQUEST FIELDS: they come from the registry row, and a request carrying `model` or `effort` is ignored. 200 returns {route,result,raw}; 403 an un-enabled route with the allowed ids; 400 a missing schema or a bad role; 429 a cooling route; 502 a session with no typed result (a zero exit that emitted no result object is a FAILURE, not a success); 504 a timeout. GET /healthz lists the enabled routes. The service runs as a dedicated unprivileged account that is never `hub`, with read-only tool use and no --dangerously-* flag anywhere, and gives each request its own 0700 scratch working directory. NOT PROVIDED: any path that reaches this from the LAN; --bare (it ignores the OAuth token and needs an API key); an unconstrained answer. LATENCY: the subscription forbids --bare, so full startup is paid per call - measured 2026-09-09 on the dev PC at ~1.6-2.2s of non-model startup and ~3-4s wall for the cheapest call; the hub is slower. Callers must not put this on a sub-second synchronous path.

v1 panel presence signal (SR-020, SN-015). The shell WRITES {$WALL_PRESENCE_FILE} (default /run/wall-presence/state.json), the wall image READS it: a single JSON object {"schemaVersion":1, "presence":"present"|"absent", "observedAt":<epoch ms>, "ttlMs":<positive int>, "source":"<free text>"}, rewritten atomically at least as often as ttlMs. WHY A FILE AND NOT THE SENSOR SOCKET: /run/wall-sensors/service.sock checks SO_PEERCRED against the panel uid and refuses every other caller, root included, so the root-run power path must not become a second client of the camera owner. Ownership stays split - the app senses and concludes, the image powers. THE READER FAILS SAFE IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY: absence is believed solely when a fresh, well-formed, schemaVersion-1 file says "absent"; a missing file, an unreadable one, bad JSON, a wrong schemaVersion, a missing/non-numeric observedAt, a non-positive ttlMs, a reading older than its own ttlMs, a timestamp more than 120 s in the future, or any other presence word all read as PRESENT. Consequence, and it is the designed one: an image whose shell does not yet write this file never dims and never suspends on absence, so the feature is inert rather than dangerous until the writer exists. NOT PROVIDED BY THE IMAGE: any attention/face/bluetooth detail - only present/absent crosses this boundary.

v1 AI-usage gauge feed (SR-021, SN-016). POST {$AI_USAGE_FEED_URL} with kind="gauge" and the tightened 2026-09 wire shape: id (the upsert key), label, icon, unit="%", value, min=0, max=100, target=0, window{start,end,kind}, direction="up", observed_at. VALUE AND TARGET ARE ALWAYS PRESENT - omitted is a 400 and formerly stored a fabricated 0. MIN/MAX ARE ALWAYS SENT - omission only infers a range for units with an agreed width, and % is not one. DIRECTION IS SENT IF AND ONLY IF WINDOW IS - required with, refused without. NUMBERS ONLY: no severity, no css, no colour, ever - NagLight owns severity and the panel renders it. Five gauge ids: ai-usage-codex (weekly), ai-usage-claude-session (5h), ai-usage-claude-weekly, ai-usage-opencode-weekly, ai-usage-opencode-monthly. observed_at is when the value was TRUE: a source that fails reposts its last real reading at its ORIGINAL stamp and so goes stale on NagLight's horizon (weekly 24h, daily 36h, monthly 48h), and a source that has never succeeded posts a gauge with NO observed_at, which is stale on arrival. THAT IS HOW 'UNAVAILABLE' IS SAID - the feeder never posts a fresh number it did not measure. The timer runs every 10 minutes because the tightest horizon in play is the weekly 24h one. NOT PROVIDED: a Gemini gauge (deferred as E11); OpenCode's `rolling` bucket, which names no window length and for which the endpoint supplies none - a window this repo would have to invent.

v1 weight gauge feed (SR-022, SN-040). POST {$WEIGHT_FEED_URL} with kind="gauge", id="weight" - THE SAME ID NagLight's own feeders/weight-manual.ps1 posts, so this REPLACES that manual feed by upsert rather than standing a second bar beside it - label="Weight", icon="scale", unit="lb", value, target, observed_at. THREE DIFFERENCES FROM IF-013, EACH A 400 OR A SILENT LIE IF WRONG. (1) NO min/max: `lb` is the ONE unit NagLight infers a range for (internal/gauge.unitRangeSpan, a 50 lb bar centred on the goal, SN-040), so omitting both asks the tracker for the agreed bar and computing goal+/-25 here would put a second range authority on the producer side. (2) NO window and therefore NO direction: a goal is a standing line measured against on any day, not a pace across a period, and NagLight REFUSES a direction without a window. (3) observed_at is an RFC3339 STRING, not IF-013's integer - getting it wrong renders as a permanently stale gauge rather than failing loudly. VALUE AND TARGET ARE ALWAYS PRESENT - omitted is a 400 and formerly stored a fabricated 0, and 0 lb against a 180 lb goal is the exact catastrophic reading the 2026-09 tightening was made for. NUMBERS ONLY: no severity, no css, no colour, ever. TARGET IS THE GOAL AND THE GOAL COMES FROM THE USER'S DEFINITIONS - the `target` field of one item (located by WEIGHT_ITEM_CATEGORY / WEIGHT_ITEM_ID, defaults Health / weigh-in), which must also declare `unit: lb` or the feeder refuses without converting. `target` and `unit` are existing item columns, so no NagLight change is needed and the goal survives sheet mode. NO GOAL MEANS NO POST AT ALL, which is a different refusal from no source: no source posts an unavailable gauge, no goal posts nothing, because the target line IS the goal. No window means NagLight's `static` 7-day horizon, so the timer runs every 15 minutes to make an absent source visible within the quarter-hour rather than the week. THE VENDOR READING IS NOW PROVIDED. Google Health API v4 was verified as real and reachable on 2026-09-09 (discovery revision 20260907) and an AUTHENTICATED GET /v4/users/me/dataTypes/weight/dataPoints returned HTTP 200 with one data point the same day, so the feeder carries a parser written against that observed body: top-level key dataPoints (PLURAL - earlier prose here guessed dataPoint), weight.weightGrams in GRAMS converted by the exact international-pound definition, and observed_at taken from weight.sampleTime.physicalTime. The LATEST point by physicalTime is posted, never the first in the array. weight.sampleTime.civilTime names a DIFFERENT CALENDAR DAY from physicalTime (utcOffset -18000s), and any future consumer needing the reading's day must use it. An account with nothing logged returns 200 with no points and posts the unavailable gauge, never a reading of 0. The scope is googlehealth.health_metrics_and_measurements.readonly - there is NO weight-specific scope, and that one also grants blood glucose, body fat and heart-rate metrics. THE SHEET-MODE DEPENDENCY IS RESOLVED AND NO LONGER NEEDS A NagLight CHANGE: the goal moved on 2026-09-09 from a top-level `weight_goal_lb` key, which internal/defsheet dropped as an unknown column on every regeneration, onto the weigh-in item's own `target`/`unit`, which are existing item columns that round-trip through sheet mode today.
